title: In Trouble and in Grief, O God
description: In Trouble and in Grief, O God in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 334, “Resignation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In trou-ble and in grief, O God, Thy smile hath cheered my way; And joy hath bud-ded from each thorn That round my foot-steps lay.

lines: In trouble and in grief, O God,
Thy smile hath cheered my way;
And joy hath budded from each thorn
The hours of pain have yielded good
As herbs, though scentless when entire,
The oak strikes deeper as its boughs
So life's tempestuous storms the more
Have fixed my heart in heaven.
All gracious Lord! whate'er my lot
I'll welcome still the heaviest grief
That brings me near to Thee.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
